key_insight: A threshold-based Bernoulli Naïve Bayes framework can turn continuous medical data into clear, rule-based predictions while staying interpretable and reproducible.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help clinicians and health systems use AI models that are easier to explain, audit, and reproduce than black-box classifiers.
method: Used supervised chi-square-guided binarization to find outcome-linked thresholds in continuous variables.
Applied Bernoulli Naïve Bayes to the binarized features for transparent classification.
Evaluated calibration with leakage-safe cross-validation and post-hoc beta calibration.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark datasets, the model reported AUCs of 0.800 for Pima Indians Diabetes, 0.984 for Wisconsin Breast Cancer, and 0.919 for Heart Failure Prediction, with calibration improvements after beta calibration.
watch_item: Thresholds are learned from the training data, so performance and interpretability should be re-checked on external datasets before real-world use.
paper_title: A Transportable Threshold-Based Framework for Interpretable Classification of Medical Data
